questionText:
Consider an array $X$ that contains $n$ positive integers. A subarray of $X$ is defined to be a sequence of array locations with consecutive indices.

The C code snippet given below has been written to compute the length of the longest subarray of $X$ that contains at most two distinct integers. The code has two missing expressions labelled $(P)$ and $(Q)$.

Which one of the following options gives the CORRECT missing expressions?

(Hint: At the end of the $i$-th iteration, the value of `len1` is the length of the longest subarray ending with `X[i]` that contains all equal values, and `len2` is the length of the longest subarray ending with `X[i]` that contains at most two distinct values.)
explanation:
Step 1: Understand the state variables
At the end of the $i$-th iteration:
- `len1` is the length of the longest subarray ending at $X[i]$ that contains all equal values.
- `len2` is the length of the longest subarray ending at $X[i]$ that contains at most two distinct values.
- `first` holds the value of the previous element $X[i-1]$.

Step 2: Determine expression $(P)$
When $X[i] == \text{second}$, $X[i]$ is different from `first` (since $X[i] \neq \text{first}$).
Since $X[i] \neq X[i-1]$, the current sequence of identical elements breaks, so `len1` resets to $1$ for $X[i]$.
Therefore, $(P) = 1$.

Step 3: Determine expression $(Q)$
When $X[i]$ is a third distinct value (neither `first` nor `second`), the new subarray ending at $X[i]$ with at most 2 distinct elements can only include the preceding contiguous block of equal elements (of length `len1`) plus the current element $X[i]$.
Therefore, the new length `len2` becomes $\text{len1} + 1$.
So, $(Q) = \text{len1}+1$.

Conclusion:
$(P) = 1$ and $(Q) = \text{len1}+1$, which matches Option (B).
